snapshots.title: sentry import global silently drops all but one ProjectKey per project
snapshots.body:
## Environment

Sentry self-hosted **26.7.2**. Import target: a freshly `sentry upgrade`d, otherwise empty database (Postgres 14.23 + Redis).

## What happens

`sentry import global <export.json>` exits 0, logs `import_by_model.successfully_imported` for `sentry.projectkey`, writes **zero** entries to `--findings-file`, and emits no warning, conflict or duplicate — but only **one ProjectKey per project** lands in the database.

An export containing 18 project keys across 10 projects (8 of those projects had 2 keys each) restored as 10 keys, one per project. The surviving row holds whichever key appeared **last** in the export file.

## Cause

`src/sentry/models/projectkey.py` — `ProjectKey.write_relocation_import`:

```python
(key, _) = ProjectKey.objects.get_or_create(
    project=self.project, defaults=model_to_dict(self)
)
if key:
    self.pk = key.pk
    self.save()
```

`get_or_create` is keyed on `project` alone:

- the **first** key for a project finds the row auto-created by the `post_save` hook and overwrites it;
- the **second** key for the same project finds that same row and overwrites it again.

Nothing is ever inserted, so a project cannot hold more than one key after an import. The `_f: ImportFlags` parameter is unused, so no CLI flag alters this.

## Reproduction

1. Create an organization with one project, then add a second client key (Settings → Client Keys → Generate New Key).
2. `sentry export global /tmp/export.json` — confirm both keys are present in the JSON.
3. Against an empty, freshly `sentry upgrade`d database: `sentry import global /tmp/export.json --no-prompt`
4. `SELECT count(*) FROM sentry_projectkey WHERE project_id = <id>;` → **1**, expected 2.

## Impact

DSNs are silently lost on restore. In the common layout where each project carries a production key and a staging key, exactly one survives per project — so after a disaster restore roughly half the SDK configurations stop reporting, and the half that still works is the half anyone is watching. The command reports success throughout, so nothing signals the loss.

## Related, same method

```python
matching_public_key = self.__class__.objects.filter(public_key=self.public_key).first()
if not self.public_key or matching_public_key:
    self.public_key = self.generate_api_key()
```

Importing into a database that **already** holds these keys regenerates the public key — silently minting new DSNs instead of restoring the originals. That may well be intended for relocation between installations, but it is surprising for a same-installation restore and I could not find it called out in the backup/restore docs.

## Suggested fix

Key the lookup on the ProjectKey rather than on the project — e.g. `get_or_create(public_key=..., defaults=...)` — so that multiple keys per project round-trip correctly.

snapshots.title: Taskworker KAFKA_TOPIC_OVERRIDES Ignored
snapshots.body: ### Environment self-hosted (https://develop.sentry.dev/self-hosted/) ### Steps to Reproduce Hey, I'm running the Sentry helm chart 31.7.1 which deploys Sentry 26.5.0, using externalKafka and kafkaTopicOverrides.prefix configurations, as my org enforces topic naming conventions. My sentry-web pod appears to be ignoring the KAFKA_TOPIC_OVERRIDES for taskworker* topics, and it's raising TOPIC_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED errors as we have strict ACLs in place. The sentry helm chart has this logic in `_helper-sentry.tpl` file: ```yaml {{- if ((.Values.kafkaTopicOverrides).prefix) }} SENTRY_CHARTS_KAFKA_TOPIC_PREFIX = {{ .Values.kafkaTopicOverrides.prefix | quote }} from sentry.conf.types.kafka_definition import Topic for topic in Topic: KAFKA_TOPIC_OVERRIDES[topic.value] = f"{SENTRY_CHARTS_KAFKA_TOPIC_PREFIX}{topic.value}" {{- end }} ``` taskbroker* topics are indeed defined in the sentry.conf.types.kafka_definition.Topic Enum https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/blob/26.5.0/src/sentry/conf/types/kafka_definition.py#L12-L113 Take this with a grain of skepticism, but my initial analysis points to [adapters.py:make_producer](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/blob/26.5.0/src/sentry/taskworker/adapters.py#L223-L241), which calls [arroyo_producer.py:get_arroyo_producer](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/blob/26.5.0/src/sentry/utils/arroyo_producer.py#L79-L116), but this chain of logic never consults `get_topic_definition(topic)["real_topic_name"]` as other Kafka producers do, for example: ``` ArroyoTopic(get_topic_definition(Topic.INGEST_OCCURRENCES)["real_topic_name"]) ``` To reproduce: 1. Configure KAFKA_TOPIC_OVERRIDES with a prefix for each topic, as shown in the `_helper-sentry.tpl` file 2. Use a Kafka user with a PREFIX ACL on topics, using the prefix configured. 3. Perform the initial "Set up the Sentry SDK" for a python project and send a test envelope to Sentry. 4. Observe the Verify section in the initial project setup: it hangs on "Waiting for this project's first error" 5. Observe TOPIC_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED errors in the logs ### Expected Result Successful ingestion and processing of Sentry envelopes. ### Actual Result Sentry-web stack trace: ``` Traceback (most recent call last): File "/usr/src/sentry/src/sentry/api/base.py", line 320, in handle_exception_with_details response = self.handle_exception(exc) File "/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/rest_framework/views.py", line 475, in handle_exception self.raise_uncaught_exception(exc) ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^ File "/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/rest_framework/views.py", line 486, in raise_uncaught_exception raise exc File "/usr/src/sentry/src/sentry/api/base.py", line 434, in dispatch response = handler(request, *args, **kwargs) File "/usr/src/sentry/src/sentry/api/endpoints/relay/project_configs.py", line 60, in post response.update(self._post_or_schedule_by_key(request)) ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^ File "/usr/src/sentry/src/sentry/api/endpoints/relay/project_configs.py", line 118, in _post_or_schedule_by_key computed = self._get_cached_or_schedule(key) File "/usr/src/sentry/src/sentry/api/endpoints/relay/project_configs.py", line 143, in _get_cached_or_schedule schedule_build_project_config(public_key=public_key) ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/usr/src/sentry/src/sentry/tasks/relay.py", line 95, in schedule_build_project_config build_project_config.delay(public_key=public_key, tmp_scheduled=tmp_scheduled) ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/taskbroker_client/task.py", line 166, in delay self.apply_async(args=args, kwargs=kwargs) ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/taskbroker_client/task.py", line 198, in apply_async self._namespace.send_task( ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^ activation, ^^^^^^^^^^^ wait_for_delivery=self.wait_for_delivery, ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ ) ^ File "/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/taskbroker_client/registry.py", line 178, in send_task produce_future = self._producer(topic).produce( Topic(name=topic), KafkaPayload(key=None, value=activation.SerializeToString(), headers=[]), ) File "/usr/src/sentry/src/sentry/utils/arroyo_producer.py", line 38, in produce future = self._get().produce(destination, payload) File "/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/arroyo/backends/kafka/consumer.py", line 838, in produce produce( ~~~~~~~^ value=payload.value, ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ ...<2 lines>... on_delivery=partial(self.__delivery_callback, future, payload), ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ ) ^ cimpl.KafkaException: KafkaError{code=TOPIC_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED,val=29,str="Unable to produce message: Broker: Topic authorization failed"} 12:53:43 [ERROR] django.request: Internal Server Error: /api/0/relays/projectconfigs/ (status_code=500 request=) ``` Kafka broker deny errors: ``` Principal = User:my_kafka_user is Denied operation = DESCRIBE from host = xxxxxxxx on resource = Topic:LITERAL:taskworker for request = Metadata with resourceRefCount = 1 based on rule DefaultDeny ``` Here's a Kibana visualisation of affected topics using broker topic DENY logs against our Kafka
